title: Particulate Nature of Matter
seo_title: Secondary 1 Science: Particle Model of Matter Worksheets (Lower Secondary Science with Answers)
standard_code: Secondary 1: Model of Matter – the Particulate Nature of Matter
standard_text: Describe matter as made of tiny, discrete particles in constant and random motion; describe the arrangement and movement of particles in solids, liquids and gases; explain diffusion as the net movement of particles from a region of higher to a region of lower concentration; use the model to explain expansion, contraction, conservation of mass, melting and boiling (summary of the MOE Lower Secondary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 1 science worksheets for Singapore students on the particulate nature of matter: solids, liquids and gases, diffusion, expansion and contraction, and melting and boiling. With answers.
key_big: Matter is made of tiny moving particles.
key_sub: Heating makes particles move faster and further apart, not bigger.
body_html:
How to think about it

All matter is made of tiny, discrete particles that are always moving randomly.

  • Solid: closely packed, orderly, vibrate in place. Liquid: close, random, slide past each other. Gas: far apart, move fast in all directions.
  • Diffusion: net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration. Faster in gases and at higher temperatures.
  • Expansion: on heating, particles move faster and further apart. They do not get bigger.
  • Mass is conserved in melting, boiling and expansion: no particles are added or lost.
Example

Why does a metal rod get longer when heated?

Particles vibrate more and move further apart

Answer: The rod expands; the particles stay the same size.

Example

Ink spreads in still water. Why?

Particles move randomly

Answer: Diffusion from a higher to a lower concentration.

Common mistakes

  • Saying particles expand when heated. The spaces between them increase.
  • Saying particles in a solid do not move. They vibrate.
  • Thinking mass increases when a solid melts or expands.
  • Thinking diffusion only happens in gases. It happens in liquids too.

faq.a: The net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.

faq.q: Why do things expand when heated?
faq.a: The particles move faster and further apart, so the substance takes up more space. The particles do not get bigger.

faq.q: Does mass change when ice melts?
faq.a: No. The particles are the same; only their arrangement changes.

items.e: In a gas, particles are far apart and randomly arranged and move quickly and randomly in all directions.

items.q: A 80 g brass key is heated and expands. What happens to its density?
